title: KCET 2016 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The half-life period of a 1st order reaction is 60 minutes. What percentage will be left over after 240 minutes ?
questions.explanation: 240 minutes = 4 half-lives, so fraction remaining = (1/2)$^4$ = 1/16 = 6.25%.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a colligative property ?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles; optical activity is a property of molecular structure, not particle count.

questions.q: The contribution of particle at the edge centre to a particular unit cell is,
questions.explanation: An atom at an edge centre is shared by 4 unit cells, so its contribution is 1/4.

questions.q: When an electrolyte is dissociated in solution, the van't Hoff's factor (i) is,
questions.explanation: Dissociation increases the number of particles in solution, so i = (observed colligative property)/(calculated) > 1.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect in a galvanic cell ?
options: The electrode at which electrons are gained is called cathode.
The electrode at which electrons are lost is called cathode.
questions.explanation: The electrode where electrons are lost (oxidation) is the anode, not the cathode; statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q: A secondary cell is one
options: can be recharged by passing current through it in the same direction.
can be recharged by passing current through it in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: A secondary (rechargeable) cell is recharged by passing current through it in the direction opposite to the discharge current.

questions.q: Osmotic pressure of the solution can be increased by,
options: increasing the temperature of the solution.
decreasing the temperature of the solution.
increasing the volume of the vessel.
questions.explanation: Since $\Pi = CRT$, osmotic pressure increases with increasing temperature at constant concentration.

questions.q: The amount of current in Faraday is required for the reduction of 1 mol of Cr$_2$O$_7^{--}$ ions to Cr$^{3+}$ is,
questions.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons; with 2 Cr atoms per Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$, total electrons gained = 6, so 6 F is required.

questions.q: For a chemical reaction, mA $\rightarrow$ xB, the rate law is r = k[A]$^2$. If the concentration of A is doubled, the reaction rate will be,
questions.explanation: Since rate $\propto$ [A]$^2$, doubling [A] increases rate by 2$^2$ = 4 times (quadrupled).

questions.q: Schottky defect in a crystal is observed when,
options: Unequal number of cations and anions are missing from the lattice.
Equal number of cations and anions are missing from the lattice.
An ion leaves its normal site and occupies an interstitial site.
No ion is missing from its lattice site
questions.explanation: Schottky defect involves equal numbers of cations and anions missing from the lattice, keeping electrical neutrality.

questions.q: 3A $\longrightarrow$ 2B, rate of reaction $+\dfrac{d[B]}{dt}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Rate $= -\dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{d[A]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[B]}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{d[B]}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\dfrac{d[A]}{dt}$.

questions.q: The activation energy of a chemical reaction can be determined by,
options: evaluating rate constants at two different temperatures.
evaluating the concentration of reactants at two different temperatures.
evaluating rate constant at standard temperature.
questions.explanation: Using the Arrhenius equation, activation energy is found from rate constants measured at two different temperatures (KEA key also accepted option 4).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect w.r.t. Physisorption ?
options: The forces involved are van der Waal's forces.
More easily liquifiable gases are adsorbed easily.
Under high pressure it results into Multi-molecular layer on adsorbent surface.
questions.explanation: Physisorption is exothermic, so $\Delta H_{adsorption}$ is low and negative, not positive; statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q: Sulphur sol contains
questions.explanation: A sulphur sol is a colloid formed of large aggregates of S$_8$ molecules dispersed in water.

questions.q: Reactions in Zeolite catalyst depend on,
questions.explanation: Shape-selective catalysis in zeolites depends on pore size, aperture size, and cavity size together.

questions.q: IUPAC name of the compound H$_3$C-CH=CH-CH$_2$Br [but-2-ene with a bromomethyl group replacing one terminal H] is,
questions.explanation: The structure CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_2$Br is numbered to give the double bond the lowest locant: 1-bromobut-2-ene.

questions.q: Replacement of Cl of Chlorobenzene to give phenol requires drastic conditions, but Cl of 2, 4 - dinitro chlorobenzene is readily replaced. This is because,
options: $-$NO$_2$ group makes the ring electron rich at ortho and para positions.
$-$NO$_2$ group withdraws electrons from meta position.
$-$NO$_2$ withdraws electrons from ortho and para positions.
questions.explanation: The $-$NO$_2$ groups withdraw electron density from the ortho/para carbon bearing Cl, stabilising the intermediate and favouring nucleophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q: In the reaction : Ethanol $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ X $\xrightarrow{\text{alc KOH}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4,\ \text{Room temp.}\ /\ \text{H}_2\text{O},\ \Delta}$ Z, the product Z is,
questions.explanation: X = ethyl chloride, Y = ethene (elimination by alc. KOH); ethene reacts with cold conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at room temperature to give ethyl hydrogen sulphate, CH$_3$CH$_2$OSO$_3$H (as per KEA key; a grace mark was awarded, likely due to the ambiguous double condition printed over the last arrow).

questions.q: Which of the following compound is most acidic ?
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing $-$NO$_2$ group in o-nitrophenol stabilises the phenoxide ion strongly, making it the most acidic among the choices.

questions.q: Benzene carbaldehyde is reacted with concentrated NaOH solution to give the products A and B. The product A can be used food preservative and the product B is an aromatic hydroxy compound where OH group is linked to sp$^3$ hybridised carbon atom next to Benzene ring. The products A and B are respectively,
questions.explanation: This is the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde: it disproportionates in conc. NaOH to give sodium benzoate (A) and benzyl alcohol/phenylmethanol (B).

questions.q: The reaction which involves dichlorocarbene as an electrophile is,
questions.explanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with CHCl$_3$/NaOH generating electrophilic dichlorocarbene ($:$CCl$_2$), which attacks the phenoxide ring.

questions.q: Ethanol is converted into ethoxy ethane,
options: by heating excess of ethanol with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 140 °C.
by heating Ethanol with excess of conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 443 K.
by treating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at room temperature.
by treating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at 273 K.
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether is obtained by heating excess ethanol with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ at about 140 °C (Williamson-type dehydration); excess acid at higher temperature instead gives ethene.

questions.q: An organic compound X is oxidised by using acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ solution. The product obtained reacts with phenyl hydrazine but does not answer silver mirror test. The compound X is,
questions.explanation: 2-Propanol is oxidised to acetone (a ketone), which forms a phenylhydrazone but gives a negative Tollens' (silver mirror) test, unlike an aldehyde.

questions.q: Predict the product 'C' in the following series of reactions : CH$_3$$-$COOH $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ A $\xrightarrow[\text{Anhyd AlCl}_3]{\text{C}_6\text{H}_6}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}}$ C
questions.explanation: A = CH$_3$COCl, B = acetophenone (C$_6$H$_5$COCH$_3$) via Friedel-Crafts acylation, and Grignard addition of CH$_3$MgBr to the ketone gives the tertiary alcohol (CH$_3$)$_2$C(OH)C$_6$H$_5$ (grace mark was awarded for this question).

questions.q: The number of oxygen atoms in 4.4 gm of CO$_2$ is,
questions.explanation: Moles of CO$_2$ = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol, giving 0.2 mol O atoms = $1.2 \times 10^{23}$ atoms.

questions.q: If the bond energies of H$-$H, Br$-$Br and H$-$Br are 433, 192 and 364 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively, then $\Delta H\degree$ for the reaction : H$_2$(g) + Br$_2$(g) $\rightarrow$ 2HBr(g) is
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Sigma$(bonds broken) $- \Sigma$(bonds formed) = (433+192) $-$ 2(364) = 625 $-$ 728 = $-103$ kJ.

questions.q: In the reaction; Fe(OH)$_3$(s) $\rightleftharpoons$ Fe$^{3+}$(aq) + 3OH$^-$(aq), if the concentration of OH$^-$ ions is decreased by $\dfrac{1}{4}$ times, then the equilibrium concentration of Fe$^{3+}$ will increase by,
questions.explanation: K$_{sp}$ = [Fe$^{3+}$][OH$^-$]$^3$ is constant; if [OH$^-$] becomes 1/4, [Fe$^{3+}$] must increase by $4^3$ = 64 times to keep K$_{sp}$ constant.

questions.q: The correct statement regarding entropy is,
options: At absolute zero temperature, entropy of a perfectly crystalline solid is zero.
At absolute zero temperature, the entropy of a perfectly crystalline substance is +Ve.
At absolute zero temperature, the entropy of all crystalline substances is zero.
At 0 °C, the entropy of a perfect crystalline solid is zero.
questions.explanation: This is the third law of thermodynamics: the entropy of a perfectly crystalline solid is zero at absolute zero (0 K).

questions.q: Equilibrium constants K$_1$ and K$_2$ for the following equilibria (a) NO(g) + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ NO$_2$(g) (b) 2NO$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO(g) + O$_2$(g) are related as :
questions.explanation: Reaction (b) is the reverse of 2 $\times$ reaction (a); doubling (a) squares K$_1$, and reversing inverts it, giving $K_2 = 1/K_1^2$.

questions.q: Van-Arkel method of refining Zirconium involves,
options: removing all oxygen and nitrogen impurities.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Impure Zr is converted to volatile ZrI$_4$ which decomposes on a hot filament to pure Zr, leaving oxygen and nitrogen impurities behind.

questions.q: The composition of 'copper matte' is,
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Copper matte, obtained during smelting, is a mixture of Cu$_2$S and FeS.

questions.q: The complex formed when Al$_2$O$_3$ is leached from Bauxite using concentrated NaOH solution is,
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In the Bayer process, Al$_2$O$_3$ dissolves in hot conc. NaOH to form soluble sodium aluminate, Na[Al(OH)$_4$].

questions.q: The property which is not true about Fluorine is,
options: Most of its reactions are exothermic.
It forms only one oxo acid.
questions.explanation: Due to strong lone pair-lone pair repulsion between small F atoms, the F$-$F bond is actually weak; so "high bond dissociation enthalpy" is not true.

questions.q: Which is true regarding nitrogen ?
options: Ability to form p$\pi$ - p$\pi$ bonds with itself
questions.explanation: Small size and absence of d-orbitals allow nitrogen to form strong p$\pi$-p$\pi$ multiple bonds with itself, as in N$_2$.

questions.q: The shape of XeF$_6$ is,
questions.explanation: XeF$_6$ has 6 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (AX$_6$E), giving a distorted octahedral shape.

questions.q: The number of isomers possible for the octahedral complex [CoCl$_2$(en)(NH$_3$)$_2$]$^+$ is,
questions.note: The standard count is three isomers: a trans (achiral) form plus a cis form that is chiral (a pair of optical enantiomers) = 1 + 2 = 3. The KEA key credits option (4), four isomers.
questions.explanation: The complex [CoCl$_2$(en)(NH$_3$)$_2$]$^+$ shows cis/trans geometrical isomerism, with the cis form additionally being chiral (optically active); KEA's key credits four isomers as the answer.

questions.q: CO is a stronger ligand than Cl$^-$, because
questions.explanation: CO is a strong-field ligand because its empty $\pi^*$ orbitals accept back-donated electron density from the metal ($\pi$-acceptor behaviour).

questions.q: The bivalent metal ion having maximum paramagnetic behaviour among the first transition series elements is,
questions.explanation: Mn$^{2+}$ (3d$^5$) has 5 unpaired electrons, the maximum among the given bivalent ions, giving it the highest paramagnetism.

questions.q: When a brown compound of Mn (A) is treated with HCl, it gives a gas (B). The gas (B) taken in excess reacts with NH$_3$ to give an explosive compound (C). The compounds A, B and C are;
options: A = MnO, B = Cl$_2$, C = NH$_4$Cl
questions.explanation: MnO$_2$ + conc. HCl gives Cl$_2$ gas; excess Cl$_2$ with NH$_3$ gives the explosive nitrogen trichloride, NCl$_3$.

questions.q: Mn$^{2+}$ compounds are more stable than Fe$^{2+}$ compounds towards oxidation to their +3 state, because
options: Mn$^{2+}$ is more stable with high 3rd Ionisation energy.
questions.explanation: Mn$^{2+}$ (3d$^5$, half-filled and extra stable) has a high third ionisation energy, so it resists oxidation to Mn$^{3+}$ more than Fe$^{2+}$ resists oxidation to Fe$^{3+}$.

questions.q: Which of the following sequence is correct regarding field strength of ligands as per spectrochemical series ?
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series, field strength increases as SCN$^-$ < F$^-$ < ... < CN$^-$ < CO, with CO and CN$^-$ being the strongest field ligands.

questions.q: As per IUPAC norms, the name of the complex [Co(en)$_2$(ONO)Cl]Cl is
options: Chlorido di(ethylene diamine) nitro cobalt (III) chloride.
questions.explanation: Ligands are cited alphabetically as chlorido, bis(ethane-1,2-diamine), nitrito-O-, giving option (1); a grace mark was awarded for this question, likely due to the imprecise "nitro-o" wording in the options.

questions.q: In the following sequence of reactions ; A $\xrightarrow{\text{Reduction}}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{HNO}_2}$ CH$_3$CH$_2$OH. The compound A is
questions.explanation: Ethane nitrile (CH$_3$CN) is reduced to ethanamine (CH$_3$CH$_2$NH$_2$), which reacts with HNO$_2$ to give ethanol.

questions.q: An organic compound A on reduction gives compound B, which on reaction with trichloromethane and caustic potash forms C. The compound 'C' on catalytic reduction gives N–methyl benzenamine, the compound 'A' is,
questions.explanation: Nitrobenzene (A) is reduced to aniline (B); the carbylamine reaction (CHCl$_3$/KOH) converts B to phenyl isocyanide (C), whose reduction gives N-methylaniline.

questions.q: Which of the following gives positive Fehling's solution test ?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a reducing sugar with a free aldehyde group and gives a positive Fehling's test; sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

questions.q: A liquid can exist only,
options: Between triple point and critical point.
At any temperature above melting point.
Between melting point and critical point.
questions.explanation: The liquid state exists only in the temperature/pressure range between the triple point and the critical point of the substance.

questions.q: The energy of electron in the n$^{th}$ Bohr orbit of H-atom is
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen atom, the energy of the electron in the n$^{th}$ Bohr orbit is $E_n = -13.6/n^2$ eV.

questions.q: Consider the following sets of quantum numbers : Which of the below setting is not permissible arrangement of electrons in an atom ?
questions.explanation: For l=2, the magnetic quantum number m can only range from $-2$ to $+2$; m=$-3$ is not allowed, making option (4) impermissible.

questions.q: The increasing order of bond order of O$_2$, O$_2^+$, O$_2^-$ and O$_2^{--}$ is
HCl gas is covalent and NaCl is an ionic compound. This is because
options: Electronegativity difference between H and Cl is less than 2.1.
questions.explanation: A small electronegativity difference (H-Cl, < 2.1) favours covalent bonding, while the large Na-Cl difference favours ionic bonding.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true ?
options: In vulcanisation the rubber becomes harder and stronger.
Natural rubber has 'trans' configuration at every double bond.
Buna-S is a co-polymer of Butene and styrene.
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is actually cis-1,4-polyisoprene (not trans, that is gutta-percha); the KEA key also accepted options 3 and 4 as "not true" statements, likely because Buna-S is really a copolymer of buta-1,3-diene (not butene) with styrene.

questions.q: Which of the following is a polyamide ?
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is formed by amide linkages between hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, making it a polyamide.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about H-bonding in DNA ?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine (2 H-bonds) and guanine pairs with cytosine (3 H-bonds).

questions.q: Which of the following is employed as Tranquilizer ?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Equanil (meprobamate) is used as a tranquilizer; Naproxen is an analgesic, Tetracycline an antibiotic, and Dettol an antiseptic.

questions.q: Reactivity of order of halides for dehydrohalogenation is
options: R – F > R – Cl > R – Br > R – I
R – I > R – Br > R – Cl > R – F
R – I > R – Cl > R – Br > R – F
R – F > R – I > R – Br > R – Cl
questions.explanation: The weaker C$-$I bond breaks most easily, so reactivity for elimination follows R$-$I > R$-$Br > R$-$Cl > R$-$F.

questions.q: Main axis of diatomic molecule is Z. The orbitals P$_x$ and P$_y$ overlap to form
questions.explanation: P$_x$ and P$_y$ are perpendicular to the Z internuclear axis and to each other; side-on overlap of parallel p-orbitals (e.g. P$_x$-P$_x$) gives a $\pi$ bond, though since P$_x$ and P$_y$ are mutually perpendicular their net overlap is actually zero (the KEA key accepted both options 1 and 4).

questions.q: The hybridisation of C in diamond, graphite and ethyne is in the order
questions.explanation: Carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised in diamond, sp$^2$ in graphite, and sp in ethyne (triple bond).

questions.q: A miscible mixture of C$_6$H$_6$ + CHCl$_3$ can be separated by
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Benzene and chloroform are miscible liquids with different boiling points, so they are separated by distillation.

questions.q: An organic compound contains C = 40%, H = 13.33% and N = 46.67%. Its emperical formula is
questions.explanation: Moles: C=40/12=3.33, H=13.33/1=13.33, N=46.67/14=3.33; ratio C:H:N = 1:4:1, giving the empirical formula CH$_4$N.

questions.q: Electrophile that participates in nitration of benzene is
questions.explanation: In nitration of benzene, conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ and HNO$_3$ generate the nitronium ion, NO$_2^+$, which is the actual electrophile.
